name: San Andrés y Sauces (Spain)
description: A yellow saltire on a field divided per saltire, green above and below and red at the hoist and fly.
history: The flag of San Andrés y Sauces was approved by order of 2 August 2013 of the Government of the Canary Islands, published in the Boletín Oficial de Canarias of 9 August 2013: a rectangular flag with a length of three halves of its width, bearing a yellow saltire or cross of Saint Andrew whose ends reach the corners of the cloth and whose arms are a fifth of the width of the cloth; if the flag bears the arms they are placed at the geometric centre at half the height. The flag, which takes the three colours of the municipal arms, represents the two elements of the municipality's name: San Andrés by the cross of that saint, and Sauces (willows) by the green colour characteristic of those trees.

features.role: saltire reaching the corners, a fifth of the width
